text:
maria (prod): kicking off a small WG to align enterprise compliance roadmap decisions — audit logs, BYOK/KMS, SOC2 evidence, and retention buckets.  Goal: clear launch gates by EOW next sprint.
kevin (eng): SGTM. can we prioritize the things that block Dedicated/Private customers first? those are the asks we keep hearing.
ashley (security): +1. blocking items from a security POV: (1) tenant-scoped audit logs with tamper-evidence, (2) BYOK handshake + rotation policy, (3) retention + legal-hold override.
samir (ops): also needs: operational runbooks for evidence export and incident retrieval SLA. we can't commit to enterprise SLAs until runbooks and automation exist.
maria (prod): propose this decomposition: M1 = Audit ingestion & immutable tail (basic retention tiers); M2 = BYOK (handoff + escrow API); M3 = Evidence export + legal-hold; M4 = SOC2/ISO packaging + cert artifacts. agree?
kevin (eng): sounds good. quick trade: immutable tail (M1) can be a lightweight append-only object store + signed manifests to start. that reduces infra lift vs full merkle proofs. we can later add proofs for high-trust customers.
nashley (security): we should capture that as "tamper-evidence v1 = signed manifests, v2 = merkle/attestation" in acceptance criteria. also need KMS key policies for BYOK: key-usage-only, no cross-tenant decrypt on our side.
maria (prod): noted. acceptance criteria draft (high level):
```
- M1: per-tenant append-only audit stream, retention tiers configurable (30d/1y/7y), signed manifest for daily snapshots.
- M2: BYOK onboarding API + escrow toggle; rotation handshake documented; no plaintext keys stored by Redwood.
- M3: evidence export CLI + API (zip + checksum), legal-hold toggle that prevents GC and signals ops.
- M4: one-click SOC2 evidence bundle for last 12 months + metadata catalog.
```
kevin (eng): question: retention tiers — do we want per-route retention? e.g., short-lived inference logs vs long-lived admin events. per-tenant/per-route increases complexity. we could do per-tenant buckets initially and expose filterable export.
samir (ops): per-route would blow up storage index. prefer per-tenant tier + export filters. ops can maintain a low-cost cold archive for long tails.
nashley (security): product note: some customers require retention of admin events for 7+ years. we need ability to promote (pin) an event to long-term retention via legal-hold or export. include that in runbook.
dara (legal): from legal: need export formats to include chain-of-custody metadata (who requested, auth token, checksum, export TTL). also require a tamper-evidence statement in contracts.
maria (prod): good call. we'll add contract language template for tamper evidence + BYOK handoff responsibilities.
kevin (eng): BYOK implementation options: (A) bring-your-own-KMS integration (IAM delegated, Redwood calls customer KMS for decryption), (B) envelope keys with customer-provided root stored encrypted in our HSM -> slightly more infra. which do we prefer?
nashley (security): (A) is simpler and aligns with least-privilege if we can ensure network/security posture. (B) gives more control for offline escrow scenarios. tradeoff: (A) requires customers to allow outbound KMS calls from Redwood to their KMS. not always possible.
maria (prod): accept both patterns as supported modes. default to (A) for self-serve, offer (B) for regulated pilots. add discovery checklist to capture customer's KMS capabilities early.
samir (ops): orchestration ask: for BYOK onboarding, require a preflight check that validates: KMS reachability, key policy (encrypt/decrypt allowed), rotation window, and test decrypt. make this automated in console.
kevin (eng): we should stub the preflight API now to unblock pilots. sample response: `{"status":"ok","kms_reachable":true,"policy_ok":true}`. deploy-bot: deploy completed to staging for kms-preflight endpoint — build 2026.03.22.
ashley (security): acceptance test matrix idea: for each customer pilot, run: preflight pass, signed-manifest verified, export round-trip (export->import), legal-hold exercise. all pass => green for Dedicated onboarding.
maria (prod): roadmapping ask: who owns rollout gating? my proposal: Product signs off on acceptance criteria, Security runs validation, Ops verifies runbooks, Legal approves contract language. if any fail, feature stays in Beta.
dara (legal): ack. add a checklist item: data residency declarations per customer region must be attached to contract.
kevin (eng): timeline feasibility: we can have M1 basic signed manifests + retention toggles in ~6w if we allocate eng-sprint focus. BYOK prototype (A) in parallel as a pilot in 8–10w. evidence export and legal-hold another 4w after that. rough total 3 months for pilot-ready.
maria (prod): prioritization: 1) M1 (blocking for many GA customers), 2) BYOK pilot (sales-driven), 3) evidence export/legal-hold, 4) SOC2 bundle automation. Is everyone OK with that order?
samir (ops): yes. ops needs early involvement on M1 to design archive lifecycle + cost accounting.
nashley (security): yes, but put a dependency: BYOK must have preflight and monitoring before we onboard paying customers.
maria (prod): action items:
- kevin: PRD for M1 with signed-manifest spec + retention API (due Tue).
- ashley: security acceptance matrix + key policy templates (due Wed).
- samir: ops runbook skeleton + archive cost model (due Wed).
- dara: draft contract clause for tamper-evidence and BYOK responsibilities (due Fri).
- maria: schedule WG checkpoint next Thu 11am PT.
kevin (eng): I'll drop a stub PR in GH and ping the eng-runtime folks.
dara (legal): FYI: some customers will insist on escrow access; suggest we prepare an "escrow SLA" appendix template.
maria (prod): noted — will include as option in the PRD.
nashley (security): one more: telemetry — create alerts for anomalous export rates (possible exfil). ops should include in runbook.
samir (ops): noted. will add to runbook and hook into existing SIEM playbooks.
maria (prod): great team. thanks. quick emoji-check: :thumbsup: to proceed with action items?
kevin (eng): :thumbsup:
nashley (security): :thumbsup:
dara (legal): :thumbsup:
samir (ops): :thumbsup:
